name: netflow
description: Receives the flow records OPNsense's NetFlow export sends (version 9, over UDP) -- every interface may be captured -- and reads which interfaces the export captures on, whether each is actually exported, and which VLANs a captured interface exports again as their parent: the core joins each record to the logged connection its own interfaces name, and counts each direction of a connection once.

endpoints.name: getconfig
endpoints.survey_section: Push sources: remote syslog and NetFlow export, read from source for push sources
endpoints.note: Read-only: getconfigAction answers the OPNsense.Netflow model's getNodes() on a GET. {netflow: {capture: {interfaces, egress_only, version, targets}, collect: {enable}, activeTimeout, inactiveTimeout}}, each option list an object of {value, selected} keyed by the option.

endpoints.name: interfaces_info
endpoints.survey_section: Push sources: remote syslog and NetFlow export, read from source for push sources
endpoints.note: Read-only, called with the argument 1 (details). The standard search envelope; each row a device's ifconfig details (legacy_interfaces_details, src/etc/inc/interfaces.lib.inc). Read: identifier, device, macaddr (the ether line's address, all zeros without one: S5c) and vlan.parent (S6c).

settings.label: plugin.netflow.setting.join_tolerance_seconds
settings.note: How far after a leg was logged, in seconds, a flow record may start and still join it (PS19 rule 3 of the NetFlow join amendment). 3 is opnview's own default, the sum of the three one-second resolutions the join compares across: the filter log's timestamp is whole seconds (survey, data source 1); OPNsense's NetFlow start instant is whole seconds, the header's unix_secs and the uptime fields each truncated to a second (survey, Push sources, S10); and the normaliser reads a zone-less filter-log timestamp with the firewall's offset, measured to the second. LV-NJ measures the distribution of record start minus leg instant and confirms or replaces it. At most 60: a larger tolerance would let a record join a leg logged a minute before it began, which no resolution explains.

settings.label: plugin.netflow.setting.retention_flow_record_seconds
settings.note: How long a flow record is kept, in seconds (PS17 of the NetFlow join amendment). 0, the default, follows retention_seconds: the flow records are kept as long as the filter log's flows they join. The largest value is the longest interval a duration represents.

measures.name: netflow
measures.label: plugin.netflow.measure.netflow
measures.description: The bytes and packets the firewall's NetFlow export reported for the logged connections, each direction counted once: from the records joined to the first leg, or from the translated copies where no exporter sees the first leg's form (NJ5 of the amendment "the NetFlow join with every interface captured"). A second measure beside the logged one, never summed with it; like every figure opnview draws, it is a lower bound, and traffic between two clients behind one interface is in no figure.
